```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

## Time units

The trial duration `T`, the handling time `h` and its standard deviation `s`
share the time unit of the experiment, and the encounter-rate coefficient
`a` is per unit of time. The unit can be minutes, hours, days or anything
else: internally, funresMech measures time in units of `T`, so the same
experiment entered in hours or in minutes gives the same fit, with `h` and
`s` converted and `a` scaled accordingly. Give the unit a name for printed
output:

```{r units}
fit_h   <- fit_funres(d, T = 24,   time_unit = "h")
fit_min <- fit_funres(d, T = 1440, time_unit = "min")
# h and s of fit_min are 60 times those of fit_h; a is 60 times smaller;
# z, k and the likelihood are identical (with the same random seed)
```

## Search bounds

The optimizer searches each parameter within bounds, on a dimensionless and
mostly logarithmic scale. The default bounds are wide and do not depend on
the time unit:

| Parameter searched | Default range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `lambda` | 10^−3^ to 10^4^ | Expected number of encounters per trial at the reference density (the geometric mean of the densities). |
| `h` | 10^−6^ *T* to *T* | Mean handling time. A handling time longer than the trial would allow at most one attack. |
| `k` | 10^−5^ to 100 | Regularity of search times (squared coefficient of variation 1/`k`). |
| `cv_h` | 0 to 10 | Coefficient of variation of handling times, `s`/`h`. |
| `z` | 0.1 to 20 | Density-scaling exponent. |

Searching the encounters at the reference density instead of `a` keeps the
useful range independent of `z`: at large `z`, `a` must be many orders of
magnitude smaller, but the number of encounters stays in the same range.

When an estimate ends on a bound, `fit_funres()` widens that bound tenfold
and refits the affected points of the profile, at most twice
(`funres_control(widen = 2)`). The reliability check "Estimates away from
search bounds" reports any estimate that is still on a bound. Bounds can also
be set by the user, in natural units:

```{r bounds}
ctrl <- funres_control("standard", bounds = list(h = c(0.01, 5), k = c(0.01, 50)))
```

## The grid of z

The likelihood profile is computed on a grid of `z` (by default 0.5 to 5 in
steps of 0.25, plus `z` = 1). Then:

* If the profile does not cross the 95% threshold above the estimate, the
  grid is extended to `z` = 8, 10, 15 and 20; if it does not cross it below,
  to `z` = 0.25 and 0.1.
* Extra points are added around the estimate and where the profile crosses
  the threshold, so that the limits are interpolated from close points.

## Open intervals

An interval of `z` that remains open after the extension means that the data
do not bound `z` on that side: values up to the end of the grid fit almost as
well as the estimate. This usually happens when search times are extremely
variable (very small `k`). Then `z`, `a` and `k` compensate for one another,
and the profile becomes flat. Report the limit as open.

An open limit can also be caused by a single atypical trial. Check the
screening (`screen_outliers()`) and, if a trial is flagged, compare the fits
with and without it.
